title: Decide language, runtime, packaging, and the dependency inventory
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.1, §5.12

## Outcome
Language and runtime chosen with decisive evidence, plus the third-party inventory that follows from it.

Presumptive answer: Rust, single static binary. Native Zenoh peer mode exists only in Rust, Python, C/C++, JVM, and Go; the Codex `app-server-client` / `app-server-protocol` / `app-server-transport` crates are Rust and Apache-2.0; single-binary cross-platform packaging is required by ADR-001.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Choice stated, not offered as alternatives
- [ ] Rejected alternatives in one line each
- [ ] Reversal condition stated: a disqualifying gap in the Rust MCP SDK's legacy-revision support, or in Windows credential-store access
- [ ] Rust MCP SDK legacy-revision (`2025-11-25` or earlier) support verified against a pinned version
- [ ] Every dependency listed with license; copyleft flagged; Apache-2.0 compatibility stated

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Decide the process model, local IPC mechanism, CLI surface, and config model
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.2, §5.11

## Outcome
One of:
(a) one long-lived `oac` daemon per device hosting the Zenoh peer, identity, policy, and the Codex client, with thin stdio MCP shims that the harnesses spawn and that connect over local IPC; or
(b) a self-contained MCP server per harness session embedding its own Zenoh peer.

Weigh: Claude Code spawns its channel server as a child process; presence must survive individual session exit; key material should live in one process; local IPC on Windows means named pipes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Choice and IPC mechanism stated, with peer-process authentication named for each platform (Windows named-pipe security descriptors, Unix socket permissions)
- [ ] Presence lifetime across session exit explained under the chosen model
- [ ] CLI surface fixed: `oac start|status|sessions|doctor` plus whatever the process model needs (for example `oac mcp-shim`)
- [ ] Zero-file local default confirmed; config file optional
- [ ] Smallest design that proves v0.1 preferred, and said so explicitly

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Decide spec packaging and the MCP extension identifier
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.3, §3.3, conflict C3

## Outcome
Standalone normative document plus an MCP extension identifier for negotiation and `_meta` provenance, versus MCP-only. Choose the reverse-DNS prefix and justify ownership of it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Choice stated with the SEP-2133 rules applied: identifier form `{reverse-dns-prefix}/{name}`, breaking changes require a new identifier
- [ ] Chosen prefix is one the project demonstrably owns; reserved second labels (`modelcontextprotocol`, `mcp`) avoided
- [ ] The spec explicitly does not claim MCP as the delivery mechanism — no MCP revision defines 'external event becomes a user turn'
- [ ] Relationship between the formal `extensions` map and the `experimental` capabilities that Claude Channels use is stated

**Skills:** `oac-mcp`, `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Decide session identity, addressing, discovery, and key storage
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.4, §5.7, conflict C8

## Outcome
Opaque stable session ids bound to a device key; how Claude `session_id` (from hooks, for example `SessionStart`) and Codex `threadId` are captured and registered; what survives `--resume` and `thread/resume`; the display URI form. Plus key storage: OS credential stores with an encrypted-file fallback.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Session ids are opaque and stable; broker-native addresses are never exposed publicly
- [ ] Display form (for example `session://device/harness/id`) separated from the stable cryptographic identity; human aliases separate from both
- [ ] Capture path stated per harness, using only supported surfaces
- [ ] Resume behaviour stated per harness, or tied to the B2 finding that resolves it
- [ ] Key storage names the library and its license for Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, and Linux Secret Service, plus the encrypted-file fallback

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-security-work`

title: Decide envelope authenticity, replay defence, pairing, and authorization
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.5, §5.6, conflicts C4 and C6

## Outcome
Per-device signing keys, the exact signature scope, timestamp plus nonce window, the duplicate-suppression store, honest `DeliveryReceipt` semantics, and the pairing and authorization model.

Zenoh provides no application-layer message signing, so the envelope signature is the only authenticity proof. Zenoh `zid` is explicitly unauthenticated and is not an identity.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Signature is normative, not 'implementation-defined' (resolves C4)
- [ ] Signed field set enumerated exactly; algorithm and key format chosen
- [ ] Replay window, nonce handling, and duplicate-suppression store defined; exactly-once is not promised
- [ ] Receipt states distinguish 'accepted by adapter', 'handed to harness', and 'unknown' honestly, given that Claude Code sends no acknowledgement (resolves C6)
- [ ] Default deny; per-session sender allowlists
- [ ] Same-user multi-harness pairing on one device is zero-config; two devices on a LAN use a short code or file exchange
- [ ] States how OAC policy maps onto Zenoh ACL subjects, given that only certificate common names and usernames are authenticated there

**Skills:** `oac-security-work`, `oac-zenoh`, `oac-evidence`

title: Decide provider-facing trust rendering and outbound symmetry
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.8, §5.9, conflicts C9 and C10

## Outcome
Exactly what the model sees for an inbound OAC message on each provider, and how outbound works on both.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Claude: the `meta` attribute set for sender, device, session, message id, and reply target, with identifier-safe keys (non-conforming keys are silently dropped)
- [ ] Codex: text-input framing with a machine-generated header and a delimited untrusted body
- [ ] On both providers, trusted provenance is machine-set and visibly distinct from user- and model-controlled content
- [ ] Claude permission relay (`claude/channel/permission`) off by default in v0.1, with justification (resolves C10)
- [ ] Outbound is symmetric through OAC MCP tools (`send`, `reply`, `list_sessions`, `whoami`); confirmed reachable for Codex via `codex mcp add`
- [ ] Codex reply correlation defined explicitly, since Codex has no channel-tag convention (resolves C9)

**Skills:** `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-security-work`

title: Decide the Zenoh transport mapping and its containment boundary
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §5.10, DESIGN Zenoh transport

## Outcome
Key-expression layout, liveliness for presence, local-mode security, LAN-mode security, and the exact module boundary that keeps Zenoh types private.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Key-expression layout defined privately inside the transport; opaque session ids never map to guessable public addresses
- [ ] Presence mapped to liveliness tokens with history-capable liveliness subscribers
- [ ] Local mode: listener bound to `127.0.0.1`, explicit decision on multicast scouting on or off, no manual certificate management
- [ ] LAN mode: TLS or QUIC with pairing-issued certificates; ACL subjects restricted to authenticated ones (certificate common name or username, never `zid`)
- [ ] Stable API surface only (`zenoh`, `zenoh-ext`); any `unstable` feature used is named and justified
- [ ] The containment boundary is stated precisely enough for a lint or test to enforce it

**Skills:** `oac-zenoh`, `oac-boundaries`

title: G1 spike — Claude Code channel wake and reply
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4 G1

## Outcome
A throwaway development-flag channel server that proves the Claude wake semantics on the pinned version.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Server declares `capabilities.experimental["claude/channel"] = {}` and negotiates a legacy MCP revision (`2025-11-25` or earlier; `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy` for stdio if needed)
- [ ] A `notifications/claude/channel` with `content` and `meta` wakes an idle session as a user turn and appears as a `<channel>` tag with the expected attributes
- [ ] A second notification sent mid-turn is queued and delivered at the next turn, in order
- [ ] Claude replies through an ordinary MCP tool
- [ ] The `--dangerously-load-development-channels` interactive confirmation is exercised, not bypassed

## Fail
No supported fallback exists. Failure blocks the Claude adapter and is **v0.1 go/no-go**.

## Also record
- Timebox and what happens when it expires
- Behaviour across `--resume`
- Whether one server can present more than one logical channel

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-claude-channels`

title: G2 spike — Codex live injection into a normally launched TUI
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4 G2, §3.2

## Outcome
Proof that a second client can deliver input into a live Codex thread the user is sitting in, on the pinned released version.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] A TUI launched normally (no config overrides) attaches to a running `codex app-server daemon`
- [ ] A second client of the same daemon delivers a message with `thread/queue/add` or `turn/start` (or `turn/steer` into an active turn)
- [ ] The TUI user sees the message and the model answers it
- [ ] OAC holds no OpenAI credentials at any point; the app-server uses the saved CLI login

## Fallback
If implicit daemon attach is not in the pinned release, OAC owns the app-server and the user runs `codex --remote ws://…`. Record which path passed.

## Fail
Failure of both paths is **v0.1 go/no-go**.

## Also record
- That cross-process resume does not attach (a second app-server resuming a held thread appends silently; issue #21743) — confirm still true
- That `codex mcp-server` is deleted and must not be planned on
- Control-socket location and peer validation behaviour

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-codex-appserver`

title: G3 spike — Zenoh local peer discovery on Windows, macOS, and Linux
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4 G3, §3.4

## Outcome
Two peers on one host discovering each other, proven on all three platforms, with and without multicast.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Discovery over loopback with UDP multicast scouting (`224.0.0.224:7446`) on Windows 11, macOS, and Linux, on Zenoh >= 1.10.0
- [ ] Discovery with multicast scouting disabled, using a locally shared rendezvous endpoint
- [ ] A TLS listener bound to localhost works in both modes
- [ ] Multiple peers per host do not collide on ports

## Fallback
Fixed local endpoint with scouting disabled.

## Also record
- Windows scouting-socket binding behaviour (`0.0.0.0` with `SO_REUSEADDR`)
- That `#iface=` endpoint parameters are documented for Linux only
- Measured cold-start discovery latency

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-zenoh`

title: G4 spike — one MCP server process serving both protocol eras
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4 G4, §3.1, §3.3, conflict C5

## Outcome
Proof that one OAC MCP server can serve Claude's legacy-revision channel path and a `2026-07-28` tool path (for Codex via `codex mcp add`) without breaking either.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] The legacy path registers as a channel and delivers notifications
- [ ] The current-revision path serves `tools/call` correctly, carrying `_meta` provenance
- [ ] Neither path degrades the other across a full session
- [ ] A server negotiating `2026-07-28` is confirmed to be rejected as a channel — the constraint is real, not folklore

## Fallback
Two server entry points sharing one core. Record the cost if taken.

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-mcp`

title: G5 spike — provenance survives a lying message on both providers
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4 G5, §7

## Outcome
A message whose body text claims a different sender is rendered to the model with machine-set provenance that contradicts the claim, on both providers.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Claude: sender provenance arrives as `meta` attributes on the `<channel>` tag and cannot be forged from message content
- [ ] Codex: the machine-generated header is visibly outside the delimited untrusted body
- [ ] In both cases the model is shown the contradiction rather than the claim
- [ ] A `meta` key that is not identifier-safe is confirmed to be silently dropped, and no security-relevant attribute relies on such a key

## Fail
Provenance that cannot be distinguished from content invalidates DESIGN acceptance criterion 6.

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-security-work`

title: Capture recorded protocol fixtures from the real harnesses
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §8 Stage 1, §6

## Outcome
Recorded wire traffic from the real Claude Code channel path and the real Codex app-server, stored as fixtures that the Stage 3 fake endpoints replay.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Claude fixtures cover initialize/negotiation, notification delivery, mid-turn queueing, and a tool reply
- [ ] Codex fixtures cover `initialize`/`initialized`, `thread/start`, `thread/resume`, `turn/start`, `thread/queue/add`, and the event stream including `item/completed` and `turn/completed`
- [ ] Each fixture records the pinned version and capture date
- [ ] Fixtures contain no credentials, tokens, or private paths
- [ ] Codex schema artifacts (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema`) referenced rather than hand-transcribed

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-testing`

title: Publish the G1-G5 verdicts and the stage-1 exit decision
milestone: M2 — Stage 1: Provider and transport spikes
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4, §8

## Outcome
The five written gate results and a single explicit go/no-go for Stage 2 onward.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each result carries gate id, pinned versions, date, command transcript summary, and verdict
- [ ] Every gate reads pass, fail, or fallback-taken — never 'probably'
- [ ] Fallbacks actually taken are reflected back into the affected decisions and into `02-gating-findings.md`
- [ ] All spike code is discarded or clearly quarantined; none of it becomes Stage 3 code by default

**Skills:** `oac-gates`
